en: The Triplet on the Visible (Sanidassanattika) and the Couplet on Abandoning by Seeing (Dassanenapahātabbaduka).

Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable and non-reactive, which is to be abandoned by vision, there arises a state that is neither non-demonstrable nor non-reactive and not to be abandoned by vision, by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.
There are six under root, six under predominance … pe … six under non-disappearance.
Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable and non-reactive, which is not to be abandoned by vision, there arises [a state] that is not non-demonstrable and not non-reactive … [and so on].
A state that is non-demonstrable, non-reactive, and not to be abandoned by vision arises with a root-condition.

With a state that is non-demonstrable, non-reactive, and not to be abandoned by vision as condition, a state that is non-demonstrable, reactive, and not to be abandoned by vision arises with a root-condition. With a state that is non-demonstrable, non-reactive, and not to be abandoned by vision as condition...

States that are non-apparent, non-visible, and impinging, and which are to be abandoned by non-knowledge and non-vision, as well as states that are non-apparent, non-visible, and impinging, and which are not to be abandoned by non-knowledge and non-vision, arise with the root condition. (Abbreviated. Under the root [condition], there are three; ...
pe ... under the non-disappearance [condition], there are three.
